verdict.rationale: Rive's site says an agent can generate content "with the CLI", and its docs describe RML as a text-based way to build Rive files with coding agents "instead of working exclusively in the Editor". Together these suggest a non-GUI, scriptable workflow, but neither source documents headless operation or CI use. The open-source runtime is a developer building block for loading and rendering files, so it earns no credit here. Missing for 10: CLI documentation (commands, auth, headless mode), explicit CI/pipeline guidance, headless rendering or export in automation, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Build interactive UI, motion, and game experiences in the Editor, or let an agent generate them with the CLI.
It lets you create and modify Rive content as code, making it possible to build Rive files with coding agents and other text-based workflows instead of working exclusively in the Editor.
